title: Shop Loading Table — Daily Production Hours by Size of Plan, Insurance Claim Repairs
content:
The daily hours that divide the planned hours of an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order follow the size of the plan. The planned hours are the estimated labor hours the plan takes for the repair order together with the labor hours of every signed customer-pay addition consent on the repair order — of whatever kind, part upgrade, unrelated damage or denied operations.

## Loading bands

| Planned hours | Daily hours |
|---|---|
| more than 16.0 (two-technician minimum) | 6.5, the two-technician daily hours |
| no more than 6.0 (small job) | 4.0, the single-bay daily hours |
| more than 6.0 and no more than 16.0 | the class's labor hours per production day |

The class's labor hours per production day, used in the middle band:

| Repair class | Labor hours per production day |
|---|---|
| Express Claim Repair | 6.0 |
| Standard Claim Repair | 5.5 |
| Major Claim Repair | 5.0 |
| Structural Claim Repair | 4.5 |
| Certified Structural Claim Repair | 4.0 |
| Aluminum Certified Structural Claim Repair | 3.5 |

**Clause.** A plan of more than the two-technician minimum of 16.0 hours takes the two-technician daily hours of 6.5; a plan of no more than the small-job figure of 6.0 hours takes the single-bay daily hours of 4.0; any other plan takes the class's labor hours per production day.

## Band edges (hypothetical plans)

| Planned hours | Class | Band | Daily hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.0 | Major Claim Repair | small job (not more than 6.0) | 4.0 |
| 6.1 | Major Claim Repair | middle | 5.0 |
| 16.0 | Structural Claim Repair | middle (not more than 16.0) | 4.5 |
| 16.1 | Structural Claim Repair | two-technician | 6.5 |
| 12.0 with a signed 5.0-hour customer-pay addition, 17.0 in all | Standard Claim Repair | two-technician | 6.5 |

The last line shows that signed customer-pay hours count toward the size of the plan: 12.0 hours alone sit in the middle band, but with 5.0 signed customer-pay hours the plan is 17.0 hours.
